rules.on_page: In all 28 'partly' verdicts the crop stopped short of the passage's end because the locator's end match was weak. The part shown was printed on the page in every case, so 'partly' counts as on the page, for the part checked.
rules.one_item: Yes when every printing carries the item the story's title names, even if some printings' matched text runs a little into the next paragraph. No when the shared text is a run of separate items (a digest), or when the story chains items so that some printings do not carry the titled item. Reports of one legislature's sittings printed as one continuing report count as one item.
rules.transcription: Fact-changing (major): a number, date or proper name read as a different plausible one; a word read as a different real word that changes the sense; words, a line, a signature or table data dropped or added. Minor: garbles a reader would recognise as errors, spelling or word-form variants, near-synonyms that keep the sense, silent corrections of printed misprints, and dropped or added small words that do not change the sense.

value.selection_rule: As in round one, a story is admitted when it reaches 7 or more newspapers, and printings are counted item by item. Where a candidate turned out to be two related printed items, each item is its own group under a parent story, as in round one; in this round such a sub-story can reach fewer than 7 papers (the Commons committee report on the Prohibitory bill, 6; the settled clause, 5; the Howes' declaration of 19 September, 6). counted_item_by_item.Henry Stuart's letter: Printed in two settings: from Virginia in June and July under the heading 'Copy of a letter addressed to the frontier inhabitants…' (VGB 7 June, NYP 20 June, PL 29 June, PP and NYG 1 July, FJ 13 July: 6 papers), and from 31 August among papers sent from Augusta, Georgia, to the Governor of Georgia, as 'an intercepted letter', after two sworn depositions (PEP 31 August, PG 4 September, PL 7 September, NYG 9 September). value.method: Round three of 1776. On 11 November 2026 the owner set the rule 'every story alike': a reviewed story is described by what kind of text it is and whose account, in the papers' own words, never as what happened; sensitive subjects get no special treatment. Items that earlier rounds held back for framing are therefore counted by the year's own rule, exactly like any other item: what reaches it is admitted, what does not stays out. As before, an excerpt ends before the names of private people where it can, and stories that turn on private people stay out. Rounds one and two left out the reports of Cherokee and Creek plans, each counted by the item finder in 8 papers. Both were read again with phrase searches over all 2,319 pages of 1776 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round3.json, phrase_hits_round3.json), every hit was read, the papers in print in their weeks without a hit were searched with loose keywords (no missed printing), and every printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/batch_16.json and batch_17.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points_round3.json).

value.selection_rule: Every single item printed in 9 or more newspapers was admitted, except digests of unrelated paragraphs. Items in 7 or 8 newspapers were chosen to cover the months from January to November and the main kinds of news: congressional and colonial documents, British documents, war reports and letters. One item a paper printed again later counts as a separate printing.

Round one (release v0.10.0) admitted the stories with an item in 7 or more papers and proposed a 6-paper threshold for this year, because 1793 has only 6 to 8 papers in print at a time; the owner agreed on 2026-11-10. The candidates in 6 papers that round one listed were read again with phrase searches over all 1,751 pages of 1793 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round2.json, phrase_hits_round2.json), every hit was read, papers in print without a hit were searched with loose keywords, and every admitted printing was checked against its page scan (SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points_round2.json).

value.selection_rule: For 1793 only, a story needs one printed item found in 6 or more newspapers, counted item by item, with the two titles of a renamed paper counted once and both scanned copies of a Kentucky Gazette issue counted once. Items that need framing stay out, and items in 6 papers were chosen, as items in 7 or 8 papers are in other years, to cover the months and kinds of news: single paragraphs of news digests that add neither (the Rome paragraph of 29 September 1792, the Paris 'sullen tranquillity' paragraph) and a rumour in two wordings (Captain Hacket's report that Dumouriez had taken Amsterdam, 4 + 2 papers) were not admitted. Items that earlier rounds held back for framing are therefore counted by the year's own rule, exactly like any other item: what reaches it is admitted, what does not stays out. value.selection_rule: For 1793 a story needs one printed item found in 6 or more newspapers, counted item by item, the two titles of a renamed paper once (the owner's decision of 10 November 2026). Where several items belong to one affair, each is its own group under a parent story; a sub-story may have fewer papers than the threshold when its parent reaches it. As for the 4-paper documents of Dumouriez's defection in round one, items in 4 papers are not admitted as sub-stories.

counted_item_by_item.Genet's letter and the answer: Genet's letter of 13 August and the Secretary of State's answer of 16 August were printed together in all seven papers. They are two signed documents, each its own group under a parent, with Jay and King's statement, which the letter answers, as a third group.
counted_item_by_item.Giles's resolutions on the Secretary of: The item finder counts 7 papers and 17 printings. The resolutions as moved are in GUS 2 Mar, NGz 6 Mar, MIR 18 Mar and NHGA 19 Mar, and as the House journal of 28 February and 1 March in NGz 3 and 6 Apr, NHG 23 Apr and AHL 14 May: 6 catalogue numbers but 5 papers, because NHGA and NHG are one paper. The Kentucky Gazette prints only the debate, in which speakers quote single resolutions; votes and speeches in GUS and NGz were not counted.
counted_item_by_item.Neighbouring paragraphs and chained item: The finder joins neighbouring paragraphs of a news column into chains: the Brussels paragraph of 17 October 1792 stands beside a Rome paragraph (6 papers) and a paragraph on the suttlers of Clairfayt's army (5); the Madeira paragraph is chained to the Philadelphia paragraphs after it in GUS. Each group here is the single item. Dumouriez's address was split by the finder into five items and Saxe-Cobourg's two proclamations into four; they are one document and two documents.
counted_item_by_item.Quotations: Pages that only quote or answer an item were not counted: Jay and King's statement quoted in NGz 24 Aug, 4 and 21 Sep and in their own later statement (PG 23 Dec), and commented on in PG 2 Sep and CI 28 Aug.
counted_item_by_item.Two settings of one paragraph: The Sun paragraph of 10 April is printed with a New York introduction ('In the Sun, of the 10th April, which is the latest paper received') in GUS, NGz (1 June), PG and NHG, and among London paragraphs in NGz (29 May), AHL, MIR and KG; the paragraph itself is the same and is counted as one item.

data_issues.A second scan filed under another date: Pages 3 and 4 filed under the American Herald of Liberty of 2 July 1793 are a second scan of the 9 July issue's pages 3 and 4 (page 3 prints 'BOSTON, JULY 3' and the 9 July heading). No admitted printing is on them (page_date_flags.csv).

Most issues were scanned twice (editions 1 and 2).

value.method: The automatic families first printed in 1793 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included (story_items.py --long-running, families of 3 or more papers rather than the default 4, because 1793 has few papers in print), were split into single printed items (items.json: 10 items in 7 papers, none in 8 or more, 22 in exactly 6). The script was also run with year 1792 over the 1793 pages (items_from_1792.json); none of those items reaches 6 papers. Two AI reviewers (Claude Fable) read the items of each half of the year in 4 or more papers and proposed the stories; each item's printings were looked for with phrase searches over all 1,751 pages of 1793 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns.json, phrase_hits.json), and every hit was read. Papers with pages in a story's weeks but no printing were searched with loose keywords. Every admitted printing was then checked against its page scan (SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points.json).

not_admitted.Left out for framing: The German Creek letter on a raid on the 'valley Indian towns' (6 papers), Captain Fanning's account of the burning of Cap Francais (6), the brig Mary's report of the dead at Cap Francais (6), the civil commissioners' proclamation giving liberty to the 'negro warriors' (4), the Fugitive Slave Act (its text in 2 papers), the letter of Polverel and Sonthonax to Genet (4), the prosecutions of Singleterry and Henfield (5; private seamen) and a killing near Middletown, New Jersey (5; private people).
not_admitted.The 1793 news that no single item carrie: The execution of Louis XVI (six different accounts, none in more than 5 of the 6 papers then in print), France's decree of war on Britain and Holland (5), the French Republic's letter to the United States (5), Giles's resolutions (5 papers), the neutrality proclamation (4 papers by its own text), Washington's second inauguration (4), Genet's arrival and the addresses to him (2 to 4 each), the yellow fever in Philadelphia (no shared item above 4 papers), Toulon (no item above 4), the President's address of 3 December (4 papers, all those then in print) and the Algerine captures (Church's circular, 3).

value.selection_rule: As for 1776, 1807 and 1808: a story needs one printed item found in 7 or more newspapers, counted item by item. No item of 1793 reaches 8 papers; every non-digest item in 7 papers was admitted. Where several documents belong to one affair, each is its own group under a parent story, and a sub-story may have fewer than 7 papers when its parent reaches 7 (the rule the owner agreed for 1776 round two): Dumouriez's address (6 papers), Saxe-Cobourg's proclamation of 5 April (5) and Jay and King's statement on Genet (5). The two titles of one renamed paper (the New-Hampshire Gazette at Portsmouth; Ranlet's paper at Exeter, the New Hampshire Gazetteer and then the American Herald of Liberty) were never counted twice toward a threshold; no admitted story's count depends on them. Both scanned copies of a Kentucky Gazette issue count once. A paper that printed an item again counts each printing. A 6-paper threshold for this year is proposed in the README and was not applied.
